MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 6, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission
Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:10 p.m., on December 6, 2010, at
200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 1, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma (arrived at 5:16 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:12 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

RECESS

At the hour of 5:11 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  December 6, 2010
 PRESENTATIONS

  Mayor Kelley presented the 2010 State of the City Address.

Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

3.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

RECESS

CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

Dan Avery, M.V.: expressed concern with the item on tonight’s agenda that would allow

Rev. John Steward, Pastor of Mount of Olives Church, M.V.: congratulated newly elected

Christine Saracino, M.V.: announced that she and her neighbors are still waiting for completion

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that it is nice to stand before the Council after a very festive
evening. She congratulated Mayor Kelley and Mayor Pro Tem Leckness on their re-elections
and Rhonda Reardon on her election to the City Council.

City Council Minutes  5  December 6, 2010
 24.  Appeal of Architectural Review AR2010-99 and Minor Exception ME2010-98 filed
  by John Coon of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s October 11, 2010
  Approval of a Petition Submitted by Shawn Nikjoo of Inland Engineering, Agent
  for Dr. Fred Sahafi, to Obtain a Permit for a Side Yard Retaining Wall Ranging in
  Height From 3’-6” to 6’-10” at 27012 La Paja Lane, in the RPD 3.5 (Residential
  Planned Development Permit) Zone. The proposed plan will include two maximum
  4’-0” high retaining walls to be located in the front setback running parallel to each
  other on the existing slope. The applicant is also proposing a maximum 6’-10” high
  retaining wall to be located to the rear of the front yard setback. Minor Exception
  ME2010-98 pertains to a modification of the City’s maximum wall height standard
  from 3’-6” to 4’-0” in the front yard, and from 6’-0” to 6’-10” in the side yard

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Mayor Kelley, Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, Council Member Reardon and Council
  Member Ury indicated that they had driven by to look at the properties in question.

  At the hour of 8:29 p.m., Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing.

  Dr. Fred Sahafi, Applicant, M.V.: discussed his project and provided photographs of the
  proposed retaining wall.

  Dr. John Coon, Appellant, M.V.: presented a history of projects at the subject home and
  expressed his concern with the proposed retaining wall.

  Shawn Nikjoo, Inland Engineering and Consulting, Inc., discussed the engineering for the
  current and proposed retaining walls.

  The following expressed opposition to the proposed retaining wall and asked the City
  Council to uphold the appeal: Ronald Axtell, M.V.; Matthew Coon, M.V.; Mike Coon,
  M.V.; Cindy Coon, M.V.; Laura Duchene, M.V.; Christine Saracino, M.V.; Ron Coon,
  M.V.; Paul Niednagel, M.V.; Ron Norgaard, M.V.; Richard Cordova, M.V.; Barb
  Linhart, M.V.; Terry Yapp, M.V.; Mark Casas, M.V.; Cathy Jasper, M.V.; Stuart Jasper,
  M.V.; Elizabeth Coon, M.V.; and Judy Perlman, M.V.

  Dr. Sahafi provided rebuttal comments and restated his desire to build a retaining wall on
  his property.

  Mayor Kelley closed the public hearing at 11:11 p.m. Upon hearing a request from Mrs.
  Sahafi to make a comment, Mayor Kelley re-opened the public hearing at 11:13 p.m.

  Mrs. Sahafi responded to accusations made about her husband’s business activities in the
  City of Bell Gardens.

City Council Minutes  6  December 6, 2010
   At the hour of 11:15 p.m., Mayor Kelley closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to uphold the appeal
  and reject the project on the basis that (1) the proposed side yard retaining walls do not
  respect and preserve the natural features of the land including existing typography and
  landscaping; (2) the scale, height, and design of the proposed side yard retaining walls are
  not compatible with the existing neighborhood character; (3) granting the Minor
  Exception could be detrimental to the public health, safety, or welfare, or injurious to the
  property or improvements in the vicinity and zoning district in which the property is
  located; (4) there are potential safety issues as the current work that was unpermitted has
  created a situation where the current solution is unstable; and (5) this action is subject to
  a confirming resolution which will come back to the City Council at the January 3, 2011,
  City Council meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon thanked her colleagues for their indulgence since she is the new kid on
the block. She noted that she wanted to read a great story but in the interest of time, she will
email it to the Council Members and ask the City Clerk to include it in the Minutes (see below).
Council Member Reardon wished residents a Merry Christmas, Happy Hanukkah and happy
holidays.

  CHRISTMAS TABLECLOTH STORY

A pastor and his wife, newly assigned to their first ministry, reopened a church in suburban
Brooklyn. Excitedly arriving in early October, they saw the opportunities to accomplish
something good before them. When they first laid eyes upon the church, they found it to be very
run down and in need of much work. They set a goal, though, to have everything done in time to
have their first service on Christmas Eve.

They worked hard, repairing pews, plastering walls, painting, etc., and on Dec 18 were ahead of
schedule and just about finished. On December 19 a terrible storm hit the area, lasting two days.

On the 21st, the pastor went over to the church. His heart sank when he saw that the roof had
leaked, causing a large area of plaster about 20 feet by 8 feet to fall off the front wall of the
sanctuary just behind the pulpit, beginning about head high. The pastor cleaned up the mess on
the floor, and not knowing what else to do but postpone the Christmas Eve service, headed
home. On the way he noticed a local business having a flea market type sale for charity so he
stopped in.

One of the items was a beautiful, handmade, ivory colored, crocheted tablecloth with exquisite
work, fine colors and a Cross embroidered right in the center. It was just the right size to cover
up the hole in the front wall. He bought it and headed back to the church. By this time it had
started to snow. An older woman running from the opposite direction was trying to catch the
bus. She missed it. The pastor invited her to wait in the warm church for the next bus which
would come 45 minutes later. She sat in a pew and paid no attention to the pastor while he got a
ladder, hangers, etc., to put up the tablecloth as a wall tapestry. The pastor could hardly believe
how beautiful it looked and it covered up the entire problem area.

Then he noticed the woman walking down the center aisle. Her face was like a sheet. "Pastor,"
she said, "where did you get that tablecloth?" The pastor explained. The woman asked him to
check the lower right corner to see if the initials, EBG were crocheted into it there. To his
astonishment, he found that they were. The woman stated that those were her initials.

City Council Minutes  12  December 6, 2010
 She had made that tablecloth 35 years before, in Austria. The woman could hardly believe it, for
the pastor told how he had just acquired the tablecloth.

The woman explained that before the war she and her husband were well-to-do people in
Austria. When the Nazis came, she was forced to leave. Her husband was going to follow her
the next week. She was captured, sent to prison and she never saw her husband or her home
again.

The pastor wanted to give her the tablecloth; but she assured him he should keep it for the
church. The pastor insisted on driving her home, mentioning that it was the least he could
do. She lived on the other side of Staten Island and had only been in Brooklyn for the day for a
housecleaning job.

When Christmas Eve arrived, what a wonderful service they had! The church was almost full.
The music and the spirit were great. At the end of the service, the pastor and his wife greeted
everyone at the door and many said that they would return.

One older man, whom the pastor recognized from the neighborhood, continued to sit in one of
the pews and stare at the tablecloth on the front wall because it was identical to the one that his
wife had made many years ago in Austria before the war and how could there be two tablecloths
so much alike?

He told the pastor how the Nazis came, how he forced his wife to flee for her safety, and he was
supposed to follow her, but he was arrested and put in a prison. He never saw his wife or his
home again all the 35 years in between.

The pastor asked him if he would allow him to take him for a little ride. They drove to Staten
Island to the same house where the pastor had taken the woman three days earlier. He helped the
man climb the three flights of stairs to the woman's apartment, knocked on the door and what
followed was the greatest Christmas reunion he could ever have imagined.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht welcomed Council Member Reardon and stated that she hopes Rhonda
enjoys being a Council Member as much as she does. Council Member Schlicht reminded
residents to watch the Diablos football game this coming weekend and she announced that she
enjoyed attending the recent lighting of the menorah and the South Coast Assembly Church

Hanukkah and happy holidays.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for another outstanding
job with the Santa's Arrival event. He congratulated the newly sworn-in City Council Members
and wished everyone happy holidays and a happy New Year.

City Council Minutes  13  December 6, 2010
 Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness thanked the Council for their vote of confidence in making him Mayor
for the coming year and he wished everyone happy holidays.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley announced that she was pleased to attend the Congregation Chabad Menorah
lighting last week and it was a very nice event. She also announced that the city will host its
whooping cough vaccination clinic on January 7, 2011, at the Norman P. Murray Community
Center from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. She will provide additional details at the next City Council
Meeting. Mayor Kelley complimented the Mission Viejo Activities Committee on another
outstanding Santa's Arrival event. She reminded residents that Santa will be in his workshop
every Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. The visits with Santa are
free and parents can take their own pictures. Mayor Kelley asked staff to give the City Council
more concise agenda reports for their binders and, if more lengthy backup material is available,
staff can direct the Council to the city’s web site. She’d like to see the agenda binders reduced in
size and, in consideration of budget and the environment, she discussed the idea of an electronic
agenda via an iPad or some other means. On a personal note, Mayor Kelley announced that she
has a new grandson and new granddaughter and this is indeed a time when she is looking at
God's blessings and feeling grateful for her family and her new grand children. Mayor Kelley
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of December is caring and she
wished everyone a Merry Christmas and happy Hanukkah.
